title: Keep secrets out of your repository
caption:
Keep secrets out of your repository

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/using-secrets-in-github-actions

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Store a secret, not a password in code
cards.body: Use the repository’s secret store for credentials needed by automation.

cards.title: Give access only where needed
cards.body: Pass a credential only to the step that requires it.

cards.title: A leak needs more than deletion
cards.body: If a credential was exposed, revoke or rotate it. Removing the file alone does not undo exposure.

cards.title: Check before sharing
cards.body: Inspect logs, screenshots and commits before making them public.

title: Use a branch for a focused change
caption:
Use a branch for a focused change

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-branches

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Give each change its own space
cards.body: A branch lets you work on a change separately from the main line of a project.

cards.title: Keep the goal small
cards.body: Name the change clearly and avoid mixing unrelated work.

cards.title: Review the difference
cards.body: Check what changed before merging it back.

cards.title: Keep the record useful
cards.body: Explain why the change matters, not just which files you edited.

title: Make a README useful in one minute
caption:
Make a README useful in one minute

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/about-readmes

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Start with the purpose
cards.body: Tell a new reader what the project does and who it helps.

cards.title: Show a working first step
cards.body: Include a short setup example that matches the current project.

cards.title: Make the next action clear
cards.body: Link to usage, support and contribution guidance.

cards.title: Keep examples current
cards.body: Update the README when setup or behavior changes.

title: Turn a vague task into an issue
caption:
Turn a vague task into an issue

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/about-issues

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Write down the actual outcome
cards.body: Describe the problem and what a successful result would look like.

cards.title: Add useful context
cards.body: For a bug, include steps, expected behavior and observed behavior.

cards.title: Keep the scope visible
cards.body: Split unrelated tasks so each can be discussed and tracked.

cards.title: Close the feedback loop
cards.body: Record the fix or decision so others can follow the outcome.

title: Review before you merge
caption:
Review before you merge

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/proposing-changes-to-your-work-with-pull-requests/about-pull-requests

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Explain the change
cards.body: A pull request gives reviewers a place to inspect and discuss proposed changes.

cards.title: Show the evidence
cards.body: State how you checked the behavior and what remains uncertain.

cards.title: Keep review manageable
cards.body: A focused change is easier to understand than several unrelated changes.

cards.title: Resolve the important feedback
cards.body: Check the final version after revisions, not only the first draft.

title: Automation needs a failure path
caption:
Automation needs a failure path

A small practical step for clearer work.

Source: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/about-github-actions/understanding-github-actions

What would you add? Follow @shipstack_ for smart tools and sharper thinking.

cards.title: Name the trigger
cards.body: Decide which event should start the workflow.

cards.title: Separate the steps
cards.body: Make preparation, checks and publication distinct.

cards.title: Make failures visible
cards.body: Keep useful logs without printing credentials or private data.

cards.title: Check the outcome
cards.body: A started workflow is not the same as a successful external action.
